## Findings ledger
- [D3.DOC22.F5] The authors use Weber’s cited material as evidence for distinguishing formal from informal power and cooperative from conflictual expressions — dim: citation_move — ref: RW0077 — move: evidence — supports: Weber is cited alongside other theorists for the distinction between formal and informal power and between cooperative and conflictual power — anchor: "Power can be held formally or informally as inﬂuence or persuasion (Gramsci, 1971, p. 12; Weber, 1921/1978, pp. 956, 1006, 1112)." — anchor-b: "The fourth polarity, consensuality, concerns the degree to which power is cooperative or conﬂictual (Gramsci, 1971, p. 12; Hegel, 1821/1991, p. 343; Weber, 1921/1978, pp. 956, 1006, 1112)." — doc: em:QASWYLCG — doc-b: em:QASWYLCG — confidence: high

sections_inspected: pp. 22–23, discussion of expressions of power
pp. 25–26, “Organizational Power: Powers to Direct and Coordinate”
scope_outcomes.criterion: A retained row must identify an argumentative act performed with a Weber citation and anchor that act in the citing text.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected passages use Weber as an authority, as supporting evidence, and as an illustration in the chapter’s account of power, organizational domination, dependence, and legitimacy.
limitations: The full chapter was supplied, but inspection for this dimension concentrated on the Weber-citing passages and their immediate argumentative contexts rather than every citation in the bibliography.
The evidence-index metadata was used only for routing and passage identification; it was not treated as an independent source.
